record.context_brief: Coupling vs Dobrushin for mixing proofs
record.original_question: For Glauber dynamics of the hard-core lattice gas, what is the precise relation between rapid-mixing proofs obtained by probabilistic coupling and proofs obtained via Dobrushin-type analytic methods, specifically in terms of identifying the norm/seminorm in which the transition operator P is contractive (norm < 1) on functions modulo constants?

evidence.quote: I'd like to raise a general question: What is the relation between proofs of rapid mixing by coupling methods and by the Dobrushin uniqueness method? ... we conclude that the transition matrix P ... has norm <= beta+epsilon < 1 in some norm or other - but which norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the hard-core lattice gas on a finite graph G = (V, E): configurations are independent sets σ ∈ {0,1}^V (with σ_u σ_v = 0 for every edge {u,v} ∈ E), and the Gibbs measure assigns to each independent set σ probability proportional to λ^{|σ|}, where λ > 0 is the fugacity. The (single-site) Glauber dynamics is the discrete-time Markov chain on independent sets which at each step picks a vertex v ∈ V uniformly at random and updates σ(v) to 1 with probability λ/(1+λ) and to 0 with probability 1/(1+λ), provided the resulting configuration remains an independent set (otherwise the move is rejected). Let P denote the transition operator of this chain, acting on functions f : Ω → ℝ on the state space Ω of independent sets. P acts on functions modulo additive constants, i.e. on the quotient space ℱ = {f : Ω → ℝ} / {constants}.

Suppose that one can prove rapid mixing of this chain by two distinct routes:

(a) a probabilistic coupling argument (e.g. path coupling) producing a contraction estimate of the form E[d(X_1, Y_1)] ≤ β · d(X_0, Y_0) with β < 1 in some metric d on Ω;

(b) a Dobrushin-type analytic argument bounding the operator norm of the influence matrix R (with entries R_{u,v} = max over boundary conditions of total variation distance between conditional distributions at u differing only at v) by some β < 1 in the ℓ^∞ (row-sum) or ℓ^1 (column-sum) operator norm.

Both methods ultimately yield, for each ε > 0, a bound of the form ||P||_{*} ≤ β + ε < 1 in "some" norm or seminorm on the space ℱ of functions modulo constants.

Problem. Identify explicitly a norm (or seminorm) ||·||_{*} on ℱ such that:

(i) the coupling-based proof yields ||P||_{*} ≤ β + ε; and
(ii) the Dobrushin-based proof yields ||P||_{*} ≤ β + ε
with the same norm in both cases, thereby exhibiting a precise functional-analytic relationship between coupling proofs and Dobrushin-uniqueness proofs of rapid mixing for the Glauber dynamics of the hard-core lattice gas. In particular, determine whether such a common norm exists and, if so, give a canonical construction.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has clarified the link between coupling and Dobrushin-style proofs of rapid mixing for Glauber dynamics. Weitz (2005) and Dyer–Goldberg–Jerrum showed that Dobrushin-type conditions imply rapid mixing via path coupling, and there is a substantial literature (e.g. Hayes' "simple condition" via the spectral norm of the influence matrix, and more recent spectral-independence approaches) identifying weighted Hamming/ℓ^p-type norms in which P is a contraction. However, a single canonical norm that uniformly reconciles every coupling proof with every Dobrushin proof for the hard-core model has not, to our knowledge, been singled out, so the question is at best partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: A simple condition implying rapid mixing of single-site dynamics on spin systems
status_evidence.snippet: Shows that bounded spectral norm of the Dobrushin influence matrix implies rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics, refining the row-sum/column-sum (ℓ^∞/ℓ^1) Dobrushin conditions.
status_evidence.claim: There is a known operator-norm framework (spectral norm of the influence matrix) connecting Dobrushin conditions and rapid mixing.

status_evidence.title: Dobrushin conditions and systematic scan (Dyer, Goldberg, Jerrum)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes rapid mixing of Glauber/systematic scan dynamics under Dobrushin-type conditions using path coupling, linking the two methodologies.
status_evidence.claim: Path coupling proofs and Dobrushin analytic proofs have been shown to be quantitatively related for spin systems.

status_evidence.title: On mixing of Markov chains: coupling, spectral independence
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses functional-analytic norms (Wasserstein/Dobrushin/spectral) in which transition operators of spin systems contract.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature studies which norms make P contractive, partially answering the question.
